messages:
Casey: FYI customer reported our tool router picked the wrong tool for a refund API call — it ran applyAdjustment instead of refundPayment. Repro attached.

Sam: customer says they hit 422 and then funds were adjusted incorrectly. They sent request id: r_8f3a.

Casey: Repro steps: call /v1/support/actions with function_call enabled. Model returned tool_choice: \"applyAdjustment\". We saw no schema validation error, just silent mismatch.

Jay: can you paste the payload and the router log? might be signature collision between applyAdjustment(amount, reason) and refundPayment(amount, reason).

Casey: payload below:
```json
{"customer_id":"cus_123","intent":"refund","amount":1200,"currency":"usd","reason":"order_cancelled","request_id":"r_8f3a"}
```

Casey: router log entry: 
```
2026-02-14T18:04:59Z router INFO request=r_8f3a model=gpt-invoke tool_choice=applyAdjustment matched_sig=(amount,reason) confidence=0.62
```

Mina: ugh those signatures are indeed identical shape. applyAdjustment is internal (no external side effects) but was wired to a policy that calls payment-adjuster which changed ledger line. refundPayment should have been chosen.

Alex: do we have an allowlist for refundPayment? maybe routing policy prioritized internal tools due to lower latency.

Casey: Looks like fallback priority list: [internal_adjuster, refund_payment, legacy_refund]. internal_adjuster has higher priority during degraded payment gateway -> it routed to applyAdjustment. Customer was hitting partial gateway error so fallback kicked in.

Jay: can we repro locally? I want full call stack from the router that shows how we matched signatures.

Casey: Repro script (curl):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/support/actions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"customer_id":"cus_123","intent":"refund","amount":1200,"currency":"usd","reason":"order_cancelled","request_id":"r_8f3a","model":"gpt-support-1"}'
```

OpsBot: Incident created INC-2026-0214-applyAdj-misroute by Casey.

Mina: quick mitigation: update router policy to add explicit disambiguation rule — prefer refundPayment when intent==refund or request contains \"refund\". Also mark applyAdjustment as internal-only so model can't choose it for external API calls.

Jay: agree. Also need to add schema metadata to tools with a "preferred_intents" list to break ties. I'll open a PR with tests.

Alex: customer impact? Sam, can you confirm how many customers affected?

Sam: only one confirmed so far (r_8f3a), flagged by customer support. They requested immediate reversal; payments team applied manual refund and reconciled ledger.

Casey: Postmortem action items: 1) policy change to prefer refundPayment for refund intent (Mina) 2) mark applyAdjustment internal-only (Jay) 3) add tool signature disambiguation tests in router integration (Jay) 4) notify affected customer and document the fallback behavior (Support: Casey).

Jay: I'll start the PR and include unit test that simulates gateway-degraded path.

Mina: deployed policy patch to staging, manual tests pass.

Casey: thx team. I'll update INC with timeline and remediation. :thumbsup:
